title: The airline
intro: Ask before you pay, or call after booking. Rules differ between airlines and even between routes.

questions.q: What does a ticket cost for a baby of this age, and is it a lap seat or their own seat?
questions.why: Infant fares and age cut-offs vary.

questions.q: Do you have bassinets (sky cots) on this flight? How do I request one, and what are the weight and size limits?
questions.why: They're limited and usually first come, first served.

questions.q: Which seats can we pick with a baby? Can we sit together at no extra cost?
questions.why: Some rows can't take an infant, for oxygen-mask reasons.

questions.q: Can we take the stroller to the aircraft door? Do the car seat and travel cot travel free, and do they count against our allowance?
questions.why: Gives you a plan for the bulky gear.

questions.q: Can we use our own car seat on board? Which models or labels do you accept?
questions.why: Only if you've bought baby their own seat.

questions.q: How much breast milk, formula, baby food and water can we bring through security and on board?
questions.why: Allowances for baby food often differ from the usual liquids limit.

questions.q: Is there an extra cabin bag allowance for the baby?
questions.why: A dedicated nappy bag makes the flight easier.

questions.q: Do families get to board early?
questions.why: Extra time to settle in and stow the gear.

questions.q: Is there a changing table on this aircraft?
questions.why: Not every plane has one, especially smaller ones.

title: The train company
intro: Most of these you can ask on the booking website's help chat or at the ticket desk.

questions.q: Does the baby need a ticket, and can we reserve a seat for them?
questions.why: A reserved seat gives you room to spread out.

questions.q: Can we book seats around a table, or near the doors?
questions.why: Tables are good for feeds; being near the doors makes quick exits easier.

questions.q: Where can we keep a stroller on board? Does it need to be folded?
questions.why: Space can be tight on busy services.

questions.q: Which carriage has the baby-changing toilet?
questions.why: Then you can book seats nearby.

questions.q: Is there help with luggage at the stations, and do we need to book it?
questions.why: Carrying a baby and bags up and down platforms is hard on your own.

questions.q: Is there a family area or a quiet coach we should avoid?
questions.why: Helps everyone relax.

title: The hotel or holiday rental
intro: A quick email before booking. Ask them to confirm in writing, so the cot is there when you arrive.

questions.q: Do you have a cot or travel cot? Is it free, and can you confirm it's reserved for our dates?
questions.why: Some places only have a few, and some offer futons instead of cots.

questions.q: Does the cot come with a fitted sheet and a firm mattress?
questions.why: So you know whether to bring your own.

questions.q: Can the bedroom be made fully dark (blackout curtains or blinds)?
questions.why: Naps in a bright room are hard.

questions.q: Is there space for the cot away from the door and window? Is there a separate area where we can sit after baby's bedtime?
questions.why: A suite or a room with a separate area means you're not sitting in the dark at 7pm.

questions.q: Is there a fridge in the room, and a kettle or microwave we can use?
questions.why: For milk, bottles and baby food.

questions.q: Is there a bath, or a baby bath we can borrow?
questions.why: Bathtime can keep the bedtime routine familiar.

questions.q: Do you have high chairs in the restaurant? What time does dinner start?
questions.why: An early dinner fits around baby's bedtime.

questions.q: Is there a lift, and step-free access from the car park or station?
questions.why: Stairs with a stroller and bags are hard work.

questions.q: Is there a washing machine or a laundry service?
questions.why: You can pack lighter.

questions.q: How far is the nearest pharmacy and supermarket?
questions.why: For nappies, formula and anything you forgot.

title: Car hire, taxis and transfers
intro: If you won't bring your own car seat, ask these before you book any car at the destination.

questions.q: Can you provide a car seat for a baby of this age and weight? Is it guaranteed or 'on request'?
questions.why: 'On request' sometimes means it isn't there when you arrive.

questions.q: What type and model is the seat, and is it rear-facing?
questions.why: You can look up how it fits before you go.

questions.q: Will it be fitted for us, or do we fit it ourselves? Can we see the instructions?
questions.why: Staff often aren't allowed to fit seats, so be ready to do it yourself.

questions.q: How much does the car seat cost per day? Is there a cap?
questions.why: On a long trip, bringing your own can work out cheaper.

questions.q: For airport transfers: will the car have the right seat already fitted when it collects us?
questions.why: So you're not stuck at arrivals with a tired baby.
